title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Food & Agriculture
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: Food and Ag-ISAC: federal agencies confirmed Iran-linked attacks on exposed processing and grain-handling PLCs; sector ransomware up 62%
items.content_text: The Food and Ag-ISAC’s State of the Threat: Food and Agriculture Sector Cyber Trends report, published 3 September and still the sector’s most current baseline, ranks nation-state actors as the second-largest category of adversaries after ransomware groups. In its words, Iran “blurs the line between state operations and hacktivism while showing willingness to directly target food security, with federal agencies confirming attacks on internet-exposed programmable logic controllers used in processing lines and grain handling systems.” It describes Chinese operators pre-positioning inside US critical infrastructure, Russian state-sponsored operators exploiting vulnerable networking equipment for persistent access, and North Korean IT workers posing as remote employees. Ransomware incidents against the sector rose 62% through July (227 vs. 140 in the same period of 2025); Qilin was most active with 47 listed attacks, followed by The Gentlemen (31) and Akira (14). The report warns that AI is shortening the time between disclosure and exploitation to hours and that exposed OT and ICS components deserve heightened scrutiny. No new development reported as of 27 September.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Food and Ag-ISAC, State of the Threat: Food and Agriculture Sector Cyber Trends (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Data through Jul 2026; published 3 Sep 2026; no new development as of 27 Sep 2026

items.title: What “Qilin targets food and beverage” looks like in practice: 30 factories, six breweries, one week
items.content_text: Background (September 2025), not a new incident: Qilin’s ransomware attack on Asahi Group, Japan’s largest brewer, compromised data-center networks via stolen credentials, shut down 30 factories and suspended operations at six of seven breweries for a week, and cost over $31 million in lost revenue — roughly 42 million bottles of production. Order processing, shipments and accounting systems all failed alongside production. It remains the clearest illustration of what Qilin, the group the Food and Ag-ISAC now counts as this sector’s most active ransomware operator with 47 listed attacks through July 2026, can do to a food and beverage producer once inside. No confirmed OT-disruptive incident at a food, beverage or agriculture operator was reported between 24 and 27 September; this card is carried as context only.

items.title: Cisco’s firewall manager: Talos says a ransomware operator with Qilin-consistent tactics got in through CVE-2026-20316
items.content_text: Cisco Talos (published 9 September, updated 21 September) tracks three clusters exploiting Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center. UAT-12197 exploited CVE-2026-20079, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass that gives an unauthenticated attacker root, which CISA added to KEV on 9 September. UAT-11823 used both CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316, with tooling Talos says overlaps with Sandworm’s — an overlap, not an attribution. The third cluster, UAT-11988, logged in with static credentials via CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3, a low-privileged login flaw); Talos assesses with high confidence that it is a ransomware operator whose TTPs “were consistent with those of Qilin ransomware affiliates”, the group the Food and Ag-ISAC counts as this sector’s most active. Talos names no victims or sectors. No new development since 21 September.

items.title: Microsoft: one ransomware affiliate rotates Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT, and lists food and agriculture among its victim sectors
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published a profile on 24 September of Storm-2570, a ransomware affiliate that deploys Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT while keeping the same tradecraft. Microsoft lists food and agriculture among its victim sectors, alongside healthcare, government, energy, chemicals, critical manufacturing and others, in the US, Canada, the UK, Spain, the Netherlands and Puerto Rico. Initial access “remains unconfirmed”; after entry the group relies on remote-management tools (Atera, MeshAgent, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, NinjaRMM), PsExec, Impacket and NetExec to move laterally, and Rclone and s5cmd to exfiltrate data. This is a cross-sector, IT-side profile: Microsoft describes no OT impact and names no food or agriculture victim. Editorial assessment: it matters here because Qilin, one of the strains it deploys, leads ransomware against this sector in the Food and Ag-ISAC’s count.

items.title: CISA and the FBI tell critical-infrastructure operators to put third-party ICS integrators on least-privilege, on-demand access
items.content_text: CISA and the FBI released a joint fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators”, dated 23 September and publicised 24 September. It cites a March–April 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation firm in which foreign actors staged about 800 files of customer SCADA information, device details and schematics for exfiltration, and it names power utilities and transportation entities among the affected customers. It recommends least privilege, monitored and on-demand remote access, security requirements in contracts, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, and practised manual operations. The fact sheet is addressed to critical-infrastructure operators generally and does not name co-ops. Editorial assessment: grain co-ops, dairy processors and packaging plants that rely on an integrator for dosing, refrigeration and line-control programming carry the same exposure, so the guidance applies to them equally.

items.title: Forescout: only 13% of network segments containing OT devices are OT-only
items.content_text: Forescout’s Vedere Labs analysis, published 22 September, covers 47,700 network segments containing more than 2.5 million devices across 209 organizations. Only 13% of segments containing OT devices were OT-only; the other 87% also held other types of device, and almost half mixed OT with both IT and IoT assets. The average manufacturing segment held 29 devices, Forescout’s measure of how far one foothold can reach. Editorial assessment: in cold-chain and refrigeration environments, where building-management systems, IoT sensors and process control often share infrastructure, that flat architecture is what lets an IT-side ransomware foothold reach a production line.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: Forescout Vedere Labs research, 22 Sep 2026 (primary), reported by Industrial Cyber 24 Sep 2026

items.title: watchTowr: two unpatched Citrix NetScaler RCE flaws are being exploited; Citrix has not yet confirmed or patched
items.content_text: Security firm watchTowr said on 26 September that two distinct remote-code-execution flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway are being exploited in the wild, found during forensic investigations. As of the morning of 27 September, Citrix (Cloud Software Group) had published no advisory, CVE, affected-build list, indicators or fix; patches are expected early in the week of 28 September. watchTowr says these are not CVE-2026-19490, the authentication bypass Citrix fixed on 19 August. NetScaler 13.1 reached End of Maintenance on 15 September. Advice to shut appliances down that circulated online did not come from watchTowr, and NCSC-NL has issued no public advisory. Editorial assessment: NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door for staff and vendors into plant and OT DMZ networks, including at processors that rely on outside integrators.

items.title: Schneider Modicon M580 authentication flaw rated CVSS v4.0 9.2 (v3.1 9.8)
items.content_text: Schneider Electric published SEVD-2026-251-04 on 8 September for CVE-2026-3869, an incorrectly implemented authentication algorithm (CWE-303) in Modicon M580 controllers below application level 4.00 and M580 Safety controllers below application level 4.20. Schneider rates it CVSS v4.0 9.2 and v3.1 9.8. Fixes: M580 firmware 4.10 or later with application level 4.00 or later (EcoStruxure Control Expert V15.2+), and M580 Safety firmware 4.21 or later with application level 4.20 or later (Control Expert V16.0 HF001+). No exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: the M580 is a common process-control platform, including on clean-in-place and pasteurization skids in food and beverage plants.
tags: Advisory — Controller authentication bypass, no known exploitation

items.title: IO-Link masters from three vendors share 20 flaws, two rated CVSS 9.8; Nozomi details the attack chain
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published three advisories on 16 September — VDE-2026-014 (Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2/ICE3), VDE-2026-027 (Phoenix Contact IOL MA8) and VDE-2026-028 (Carlo Gavazzi YL212/YN115) — each listing the same 20 CVEs (CVE-2026-27546 through CVE-2026-27565). Two are rated CVSS v3.1 9.8: an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-27546) and a malicious IODD upload (CVE-2026-27565); ten more score 8.8. On 24 September Nozomi Networks Labs published a technical write-up of the Pepperl+Fuchs master covering 19 CVEs, showing that chained together they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device and the ability to manipulate sensor and actuator data. Pepperl+Fuchs fixed the flaws in firmware 1.7.8. No exploitation has been reported. Editorial assessment: IO-Link masters sit at the sensor/actuator layer of packaging, filling and dosing lines.
tags: Advisory — Field-I/O firmware, 20 CVEs, no known exploitation

items.title: One malformed packet can crash TDengine, a time-series database used for industrial telemetry
items.content_text: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542 on 23 September, a pre-authentication denial-of-service flaw in TDengine: an integer underflow in RPC length handling on TCP port 6030 lets a single crafted packet crash the database server before any login, and repeating it can hold the service in a crash loop. Versions 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5 are affected; 3.4.1.6 fixes it. It is rated CVSS 7.5 (version not stated). Ridge reports no in-the-wild exploitation and is not aware of public exploit code. Editorial assessment: where TDengine stores sensor telemetry for cold-chain or precision-ag monitoring, a sustained attack degrades monitoring and alarming rather than control itself.
